headline: Mirroring exchanges left and right at every depth
statement: Mirror a binary tree by swapping every node’s left and right child. Return the same root with inverted links.
intuition: Mirroring exchanges left and right at every depth. Swapping children locally and then visiting both children performs the entire reflection.
approach: Initialize a stack with root when it exists.
Pop a node and swap its left and right children.
Push both existing children so their subtrees receive the same operation.
correctness: Each node is visited once and its child links are exchanged once. The same operation recursively applies to both descendant subtrees, so every path made of left/right choices becomes the path with those choices reversed, which defines the mirror tree.
bruteForce: Serialize the tree with positional information and reconstruct a mirrored tree, needing additional node allocation.

complexity.explanation: Time O(n); auxiliary space O(h). Output storage is excluded unless stated.

pitfalls: Return the root even when it is None.
Both subtrees still need processing after swapping.
Avoid swapping values; the tree structure is what changes.
